Name: True Artisan Goods
Author: Campaigner
Description:
True Artisan Goods
=======================
Have you ever wanted to turn Mayor Lewis's Lucky Purple Shorts into Juice, or turn Radioactive Ore into Cheese? ...No? Well, you can now at least!

This mod provides an assortment of craftable machines that function similar to normal machines, but create flavored versions of their products! These machines' recipes can be bought from Marnie (might change this one day) for 15000 gold each. What machines do what, you may wonder?

I. Expeller Press
- Functions as an Oil Maker, but for almost ANY item!
- Config option exists to pick either Oil or Triffle Oil as the output.
- All outputs count as their normal outputs for quests, shipping, and crafting!
- All outputs share the same value, being 1.5x of the original input item.

II. Hydration Removal Terminal
- Functions as a Dehydrator, but for almost ANY item!
- Config option exists to pick either Dried Fruits, Dried Mushrooms, or Raisins as the output.
- All outputs count as their normal outputs for quests, shipping, and crafting!
- All outputs share the same value as the normal dried items.

III. Hyperbolic Barrel
- Functions as a Cask, but for almost ANY item!

IV. Gentle Crematorium
- Functions as a Fish Smoker, but for almost ANY item!

V. Liquefier
- Functions as a Keg, but for almost ANY item!
- Config option exists to pick either Beer, Coffee, Juice, Mead, or Wine as the output.
- All outputs count as their normal outputs for quests, shipping, and crafting!
- All outputs share the same value, being equal to normal Wine prices.

VI. Milking Machine
- New machine that produces Milk from almost ANY item!
- Config option exists to pick either Milk, Large Milk, Goat Milk, or Large Goat Milk as the output.
- All outputs count as their normal outputs for quests, shipping, and crafting!
- All outputs share the same value, being 1.5x of the original input item.
- Make use of the Cheese Crusher, a new Cheese Press, to keep the flavor from your milk!

VII. Miracle Whipper
- Functions as a Mayonnaise Machine, but for almost ANY item!
- Config option exists to pick either Mayonnaise, Duck Mayonnaise, Void Mayonnaise, or Dinosaur Mayonnaise as the output.
- All outputs count as their normal outputs for quests, shipping, and crafting!
- All outputs share the same value, being 1.5x of the original input item.

VIII. Preservation Unit
- Functions as a Preserves Jar, but for almost ANY item!
- Config option exists to pick either Dried Fruits, Dried Mushrooms, or Raisins as the output.
- All outputs count as their normal outputs for quests, shipping, and crafting!
- All outputs share the same value, being equal to normal dried fruits and mushrooms prices.

IX. Roe Extractor
- New machine that produces Roe from almost ANY item!
- The roe from this machine can be turned into Aged Roe!

X. Other Changes
- The most important item ever, Lucky Purple Shorts, now has the internal context tag to denote that they are, indeed, purple.
  - This means that your Lucky Purple Shorts Juice will properly be purple as intended!
- Trimmed Lucky Purple Shorts are purple as well!

XI. Config Options
As stated above, there are some config options in this mod, so it is greatly recommended that you have [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM)[/url] enabled. Additionally, there is one extra config option; Silly Color Mode. In the game, the concept of "flavored items" is already present in things such as Juice and Wine. These items are designed to inherit the name and color of the items used to make them, which is what inspired this mod (and all my past attempts). However, what happens if you had this color on cheese, milk, and so on? Things that don't normally have colors applied to them? Well, you get a very strong color filter over the item. Some items like Raisins become super dark colors, while items like Cheese become extremely bright. By default, Silly Color Mode is disabled so these colors are not present. However, you can toggle Silly Color Mode on if you'd like. Items generated with Silly Color Mode on do not stack with items made outside of this, so it can lead to a bit of clutter.


Frequently Asked Questions (by who?):

Q: Can I turn my tools and clothes into artisan goods?
A: When I was making this mod, yes; this was very much doable. However, it had many errors due to those items not being the right type of item for turning into artisan goods. This caused a lot of errors to crop up that, without extensive coding knowledge, would be impossible for me to overcome. Unfortunately, this means that hats, clothing, rings, tools, weapons, boots, rings, and trinkets cannot be turned into artisan goods.

Q: Will items made with this mod count for quests?
A: They should! The items are all vanilla items; no item added by this mod is unique to this mod. Cheese is Cheese, Wine is Wine, and so on.

Q: Can you add compatibility with (insert mod here)?
A: By default, this mod should be compatible with tons of mods. The way I have set things up is that I use item categories for my recipes. As long as a mod also uses the same categories from the base game, those items can be used just fine. If something does not work, feel free to suggest the mod it came from in the comments. I won't guarantee that I'll get around to it right away, but I'll certainly look every now and then!

Q: Didn't you upload this before?
A: Sort of. Originally a feature in Assorted Crazy Things, I wanted to expand it further. For some reason, I split it off into its own mod, so that will likely be removed in the next update for Assorted Crazy Things. Prior to today however, I did have a mod called "Milk Any Item", but I deleted it. Wanted the much more advanced (read; nonsensical) version to start on its own legs. Don't worry, I won't make another mod doing the same thing again.


Future Plans:
- Other artisan goods and artisan goods related content if I come up with it
- Pray that Lucky Purple Shorts Juice becomes a canon item in Stardew Valley
